old.name: Republic of Ragusa — the one-month Rector
old.label: REPUBLIC 1358–1808
old.hook: Senate of 45, Rector for one month — a constitution against personal power
old.text: Senate of 45, Rector for one month — a constitution against personal power EUR 15 (Rector's Palace + Cultural Museum) OPEN ALL YEAR Late morning Released from Venice by the Treaty of Zadar in 1358 and abolished by Napoleon's Marshal Marmont in 1808 — four and a half centuries of de facto independence. The Senate had 45 patricians over 40 years old, elected for one year by the Major Council (~300 nobles aged 18+); daily government by the seven-member Minor Council; a Rector who served exactly one month and lived locked inside the Rector's Palace during his term, allowed out only on state business. Visit the Rector's Palace (Gothic-Renaissance, rebuilt after gunpowder explosions in 1435 and 1463) and the Sponza Palace (1516–22) — the customs house, mint and intellectual club of the Republic. Where Old Town · Rector's Palace, Sponza Palace

old.name: 1667 earthquake · the Gradić rebuild
old.label: 6 APRIL 1667
old.hook: Why every Stradun façade matches: regulation, not aesthetic accident
old.text: Why every Stradun façade matches: regulation, not aesthetic accident Free (Stradun + Sponza) WALK Any 6 April 1667, ~08:45. An 8–15 second earthquake estimated at magnitude ~7 (intensity X EMS) flattened most of the medieval city. ~2,000 died inside the walls per Robin Harris's count (older sources cite up to 5,000), including the sitting Rector and half the Major Council. The rebuild was directed from Rome by Stjepan Gradić (1613–1683) , the Ragusan Vatican librarian and diplomat who raised funds across Europe and enforced a uniform Baroque rhythm along the Stradun. Every facade rises to the same cornice, every window aligns across 300 metres — this is regulation. The Sponza Palace, finished in 1522, survived the quake and is now also the war memorial. Where Old Town · Stradun · Sponza Palace

curiosities:Why every façade matches.brief: The 1667 earthquake and the Baroque rebuild (Stjepan Gradić). The Sponza survived: its card tells the building.

old.name: Marin Držić · Dundo Maroje 1551
old.label: PLAYWRIGHT 1508–1567
old.hook: Capon-with-oranges recipe still served at Kopun (Poljana Boškovića)
old.text: Capon-with-oranges recipe still served at Kopun (Poljana Boškovića) EUR 8 (House Museum) OPEN ALL YEAR Late morning Marin Držić (1508–1567) is the Renaissance playwright Croatia names before any other. His comedy Dundo Maroje (1551) premiered in the Rector's Palace and is still staged at the Summer Festival. The House Museum at Široka 7 in the Old Town reconstructs his working life through period interiors and manuscript facsimiles. The Držić recipe for capon with oranges, salt and honey is the dish on the menu at Kopun — the same lane, same square as the playwright walked four and a half centuries ago. Where Old Town · Široka 7 (House Museum)

old.name: Ruđer Bošković · the 1758 atomic-precursor theory
old.label: POLYMATH 1711–1787
old.hook: Boškovićeva Stairs = Game of Thrones Walk of Shame; physics history under the same flagstones
old.text: Boškovićeva Stairs = Game of Thrones Walk of Shame; physics history under the same flagstones Free WALK Any Ruđer Josip Bošković (1711–1787) , born in the Old Town, Jesuit polymath: astronomer, mathematician, physicist, diplomat. His Theoria Philosophiae Naturalis (Vienna 1758; Venice 1763) proposed matter as point-particles bound by mutual forces of attraction and repulsion — a precursor of atomic and field theory that Werner Heisenberg called "the Croatian Leibniz." Member of the Royal Society, the Académie Royale and the Russian Academy. Buried in Milan. The square at the foot of the Jesuit Stairs — Poljana Ruđera Boškovića — carries his name; the same stairs serve as the Game of Thrones Walk of Shame and as physics history under the same flagstones. Where Old Town · Poljana Ruđera Boškovića (Jesuit Stairs)

old.name: Memorial Room of the Defenders · Sponza Palace
old.hook: Photographs of the dead · the quietest room in the city
old.text: Photographs of the dead · the quietest room in the city Free WALK-IN Late afternoon The Yugoslav People's Army siege ran 1 October 1991 to late May 1992 . The defining bombardment was 6 December 1991 : 19 civilians killed in a single day, 60 wounded, ~68% of Old Town buildings damaged. Total siege civilian deaths ~116; 194 Croatian defenders + 165 JNA fatalities. UNESCO placed Dubrovnik on the List of World Heritage in Danger and led the post-war restoration mission. The Memorial Room of the Defenders inside the Sponza Palace courtyard wing is the city's archive — photographs of the dead defenders, their ages and units, in two rooms of silence. Walk through after the cathedral; leave a moment of attention. Where Old Town · Sponza Palace

old.name: Lazareti — the 1627 quarantine, now culture
old.label: GEM
old.text: The Lazareti were the city's 17th-c. plague quarantine — 10 stone halls along the shore , completed 1627, where merchants and goods waited 40 days before entering the city. Now they house the Linđo Folklore Ensemble 's summer performances, an art-house cinema and a programme of small concerts. The Stari Mlin restaurant occupies one hall in season. Walk through after the cable-car descent. Where Ploče · just outside the gate When Linđo summer Mon/Tue/Sat 21:30
